DisplayName: Branching code review and merge governance
Summary: Branch-heavy review-routing template aligned to the current process-module graph model, with explicit decision role, routed outcomes, default handling, error handling, artifact inputs, and route-specific merge governance.
ValueStatement: Makes software review routing, QA, security, architecture escalation, route-specific merge approval, default handling, and error handling explicit, replayable, and auditable.
InterfaceContractSummary: Code review is not a single linear gate; it needs an explicit routing surface that shows who decides the next lane and what each routed outcome means.
GovernanceNotes: Review routing must stay explicit, strongly typed, and replayable so later merge or governance questions can be answered from the model instead of chat fragments.
ChangeSummary: Refreshed to match the additive branch-router and multi-parent dependency model now available in the process module.
GovernancePolicySummary: Merge readiness depends on the selected routed lane, so the current graph model keeps each merge approval route-specific instead of implying an unsupported OR-join.
ConstitutionRuleSummary: Role contracts for authoring, routing, QA, security, architecture, and merge approval stay explicit even when individuals change.
OperatingModeSummary: Assisted execution is acceptable because the branching goal is to make routing explicit before deeper automation is attempted.
SimulationReadinessSummary: This scenario is intentionally branch-heavy so canvas screenshots, authoring validation, and architecture-gap review can use one realistic software-development example.
Metrics: Percentage of reviewed changes with an explicit routed outcome instead of implicit chat resolution.
Rate of route-to-lane mismatches caught by validation.
Median cycle time for repair, QA, security, and architecture review lanes.
Share of default-lane normalizations that later proved to be workflow errors.
Merge approvals with complete route provenance and residual-risk framing.
Risks: Implicit routing hidden in comments or chat.
Default-lane normalization abused to mask malformed workflow states.
QA or security lanes skipped because the route was not modeled explicitly.
Error lane ignored, leaving branch-router defects undiscoverable.
TailoringRules: Small changes may route directly to merge approval, but the router still records the outcome explicitly.
Teams may add more routed lanes, yet default and error routes remain mandatory system outcomes.
Repair loops may repeat, but each cycle must produce a new explicit routing record.
If the module later gains explicit OR-join support, teams may collapse route-specific merge approvals back into a single merge gate without hiding the routed evidence.

Steps.Title: Prepare pull request and reviewer brief
Steps.Subtitle: Implementation packet
Steps.Notes: Package the code change, screenshots, impacted modules, test proof, and release-note draft before the review board decides what lane comes next.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Accepted work item, implementation diff, test evidence, and draft release notes.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Review-ready pull request packet with typed reviewer context and proof references.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Diff summary, screenshots, changed-surface list, and rollback notes.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: The author may prepare the review packet but cannot declare the change ready for merge without explicit routing.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Pause immediately if proof, rollback notes, or touched-surface inventory is incomplete.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Authorship stays attached to the implementation owner even if the engineer changes before review.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Pull request readiness packet
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for code review, QA planning, and release-note preparation.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must name touched modules, screenshots, rollback notes, and explicit reviewer asks.

Steps.Title: Route code review disposition
Steps.Subtitle: Switch-style review router
Steps.Notes: Use an explicit branch router node to decide whether the authored change goes to repairs, QA, security, architecture, merge approval, the default normalization lane, or an error lane.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Review-ready pull request packet, reviewer comments, and changed-surface risk notes.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Explicit next-lane selection for the reviewed change.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Review notes, chosen route, and reasons for the selected lane.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Review lead owns the switch outcome and must keep the route explicit on the canvas.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Artifact recovery: block when the required review routing decision record is missing or invalid before selecting the next branch. Do not bury routing logic inside comments or verbal agreements; the chosen lane must stay modeled and replayable.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: The review lead owns the branch-selection decision and its recorded rationale.
The author reviews whether requested follow-up work is clear before the route is accepted.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Review routing decision record
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for QA, security, architecture, merge governance, and later workflow analysis.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must name the chosen lane, rationale, and any blockers or residual risks.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Repairs required
BranchOutcomes.Description: Route the change back to the author for a focused repair pass.

BranchOutcomes.Title: QA validation
BranchOutcomes.Description: Route the change into targeted QA and browser proof.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Security review
BranchOutcomes.Description: Route the change into security and data-handling review.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Architecture review
BranchOutcomes.Description: Escalate architectural consequences that exceed local code review authority.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Ready for merge
BranchOutcomes.Description: Send the change directly to the merge approval lane.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Default
BranchOutcomes.Description: Continue when no explicit branch outcome is selected.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Error
BranchOutcomes.Description: Escalate canvas or runtime authoring failures that prevent a safe routing decision.

Steps.Title: Complete focused repair pass
Steps.Subtitle: Author repair loop
Steps.Notes: Apply the requested repair scope and return a bounded fix package without hiding residual uncertainty.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Review routing decision, blocking review comments, and the original pull request packet.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Updated change set and repair brief ready for another routing decision or merge path.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Repair diff, note of addressed concerns, and any remaining risk.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Author may fix only the bounded review issues unless the route is re-opened explicitly.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Escalate if repairs materially expand scope beyond the routed review request.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Repair ownership stays with the author unless explicitly rebound.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Repair brief
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable between repair loops until the next routing decision is made.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must state the repair scope, blocking findings, and what evidence is required on resubmission.

Steps.Title: Validate QA lane and browser proof
Steps.Subtitle: Targeted regression lane
Steps.Notes: Run targeted regression and browser proof for changes explicitly routed into the QA lane.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Review routing decision, pull request packet, and changed-surface inventory.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: QA lane result with proof depth and residual quality risk.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: QA notes, screenshots, regression result, and unresolved concerns.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: QA lead may keep the change out of merge until risk is explicit and acceptable.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not convert QA lane results into chat-only confidence.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: QA lane ownership remains explicit even when rota coverage changes.
The author reviews QA failures before merge or reroute.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: QA lane validation note
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for merge approval and release readiness if the change proceeds.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must name tested flows, proof depth, and unresolved quality risks.

Steps.Title: Perform security review before merge
Steps.Subtitle: Trust-sensitive lane
Steps.Notes: Review tenant-data, secrets, and policy-exception consequences for changes routed into the security lane.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Review routing decision, pull request packet, and trust-sensitive changed-surface notes.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Security lane outcome with explicit approval, block, or exception rationale.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Security notes, decision rationale, and residual risk owner.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Security reviewer owns the trust-sensitive merge gate for routed changes.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not let merge urgency waive data-handling or secrets review.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Security approval remains attached to the role even if the reviewer changes.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Security lane review note
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for merge or release governance.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture the trust-sensitive review outcome and residual risk owner.

Steps.Title: Escalate architecture consequences
Steps.Subtitle: Non-local design lane
Steps.Notes: Review architectural consequences that exceed local code-review authority and decide whether the change can still progress.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Review routing decision, change packet, and impacted boundary notes.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Architecture escalation outcome with explicit next action.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Architecture concern, decision, and approved next action.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Solution architect owns the architecture lane and may return the change for redesign or authorize progression with conditions.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not hide canonical-model or module-boundary concerns inside informal reviewer comments.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Architecture escalation remains attached to architecture authority rather than a specific person.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Architecture escalation brief
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for ADR follow-up, review replay, and change-scope renegotiation.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture the architectural concern, impacted boundary, and decision needed.

Steps.Title: Approve direct merge route
Steps.Subtitle: Direct merge gate
Steps.Notes: Approve or reject merge when the review lead explicitly routed the change straight to merge.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Review routing decision, residual risk framing, and release-note completeness for the direct merge route.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Approved or rejected direct merge decision with explicit rationale.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Direct merge note, residual risks, and next action if the direct merge route is blocked.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Merge approver owns the direct merge route and must keep the rationale explicit.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Reject the direct merge route when review routing evidence or residual risk framing is incomplete.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Merge approval belongs to the current branch steward, not to whoever presses the button.
The review lead confirms the routed path that produced the merge-ready state.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Direct merge readiness note
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for release readiness and audit of review-to-merge governance.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture residual risks, merge conditions, and named approver.

Steps.Title: Approve merge after QA validation
Steps.Subtitle: QA merge gate

Steps.OutputContractSummary: Approved or rejected post-QA merge decision with explicit rationale.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: QA merge note, residual risks, and next action if merge is blocked after QA.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Merge approver owns the post-QA merge gate and cannot bypass QA evidence.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Reject merge when QA evidence or route provenance is incomplete.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Merge approval belongs to the current branch steward, not to whoever presses the button.
The review lead confirms the routed path that produced the merge-ready state.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: QA merge readiness note
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for release readiness and audit of review-to-merge governance.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture residual risks, merge conditions, and named approver.

Steps.Title: Approve merge after architecture escalation
Steps.Subtitle: Architecture merge gate
Steps.Notes: Approve or reject merge after the architecture lane has resolved the non-local design concern explicitly.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Review routing decision, architecture escalation brief, residual risk framing, and release-note completeness.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Approved or rejected post-architecture merge decision with explicit rationale.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Architecture merge note, residual risks, and next action if merge is blocked after escalation.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Architecture merge readiness note
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for release readiness and audit of review-to-merge governance.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture residual risks, merge conditions, and named approver.

Steps.Title: Normalize default review lane
Steps.Subtitle: Explicit default handling
Steps.Notes: Create an explicit normalization note when no named review outcome was selected and the workflow falls back to the governed default path.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Ambiguous or unclassified review state plus the review router context.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Explicit normalization note and merge-lane readiness or follow-up instruction.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Observed ambiguity, normalized lane, and rationale.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Review lead owns default normalization and may not use it to hide actual error states.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: If the state is actually malformed or contradictory, use the error lane instead of normalization.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Default normalization remains an explicit review-lead responsibility.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Review normalization note
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable during workflow audit and branch-router tuning.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must state the ambiguous state observed, the normalized lane, and why the fallback lane was chosen.

Steps.Title: Approve merge after default normalization
Steps.Subtitle: Default-route merge gate
Steps.Notes: Approve or reject merge after the default normalization lane has made the ambiguous route explicit.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Review routing decision, normalization note, residual risk framing, and release-note completeness.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Approved or rejected post-normalization merge decision with explicit rationale.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Default-route merge note, residual risks, and next action if merge is blocked after normalization.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Merge approver owns the post-normalization merge gate and cannot bypass normalization evidence.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Reject merge when normalization evidence or route provenance is incomplete.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Merge approval belongs to the current branch steward, not to whoever presses the button.
The review lead confirms the routed path that produced the merge-ready state.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Default-route merge readiness note
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for release readiness and audit of review-to-merge governance.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture residual risks, merge conditions, and named approver.

Steps.Title: Capture workflow failure and recovery path
Steps.Subtitle: Explicit error handling
Steps.Notes: Escalate malformed or contradictory workflow states into a durable error lane with recovery instructions.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Failing branch-router state, canvas or runtime symptom, and any partial decision evidence.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Workflow failure record with recommended recovery path.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Failing state, visible symptom, and accountable recovery owner.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Review lead owns the escalation into the error lane until recovery ownership is explicit.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not guess a lane when the workflow state is broken; capture failure explicitly.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: The review lead remains accountable for the error lane until recovery is assigned.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Review workflow failure record
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for process defect repair, platform follow-up, and architecture trouble logs.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture the failing state, user-visible symptom, and the recommended recovery path.

LocalRoles.Summary: Change author responsible for preparing a reviewable packet and implementing requested repairs.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Keep authorship and first-pass implementation evidence attached to the person or agent that produced the change.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: Authorship role for implementation context and review packet preparation.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Authorship role for implementation context and review packet preparation.
LocalRoles.SeniorityBand: Engineer or approved implementation agent under human supervision
KnowledgeRequirements: Solid command of the target codebase language, architecture conventions, and test approach.
Understanding of version control, code review, CI pipelines, and release hygiene.
Ability to interpret architecture guidance and convert it into implementable tasks without scope drift.
Knowledge of defect prevention techniques, observability basics, and safe rollback-friendly change packaging.
Ability to produce evidence that links what changed to why it is safe enough to proceed.
Understanding of secure coding and dependency hygiene expectations for the stack in use.
ExperienceRequirements: Has delivered production code with automated test coverage and peer review evidence.
Has decomposed medium-complexity work into implementable slices with clear review boundaries.
Has debugged at least one production issue or high-severity defect linked to code they worked on.
Has participated in release or deployment readiness discussions and adjusted code accordingly.
Has collaborated with QA and architecture reviewers to repair inadequate evidence or design drift.
DecisionRights: Choose implementation approach within approved architectural guardrails.
Stop and escalate when required inputs, access, or environment assumptions are missing.
Recommend technical debt acceptance or rejection when delivery pressure appears.
Refuse AI-generated output that cannot be validated to the required standard.
CollaborationExpectations: Clarify ambiguity with product and architecture roles before making silent assumptions.
Provide QA and reviewers with concrete evidence, not only assertions of completion.
Document trade-offs when delivery timing forces constrained implementation choices.
Support incident and hotfix response for changes the engineer helped deliver.
AntiPatterns: Treating passing local tests as sufficient release evidence.
Shipping code that depends on tacit environment knowledge no one else has.
Accepting AI-generated code without line-level comprehension and verification.
FitnessEvidence: Merged changes with traceable test and review evidence.
Examples of defect analysis or incident participation showing engineering accountability.
Consistent adherence to repository conventions and delivery guardrails.
Code reviews from peers indicating clarity, maintainability, and risk awareness.

LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: Decision owner for review routing, normalization, and escalation safety.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Decision owner for review routing, normalization, and escalation safety.
LocalRoles.SeniorityBand: Senior staff engineer, QA lead, or delegated review authority
KnowledgeRequirements: Ability to design risk-based test strategy across functional, regression, integration, and exploratory layers.
Knowledge of evidence quality, reproducibility, and how to communicate remaining uncertainty honestly.
Understanding of production-like environment limitations and how they affect release confidence.
Ability to challenge weak acceptance criteria or under-scoped implementation evidence.
Knowledge of defect taxonomy, escape analysis, and prioritization under release pressure.
Ability to connect customer impact and business criticality to appropriate validation depth.
ExperienceRequirements: Has owned test strategy for medium or high-risk releases with documented go/no-go input.
Has triaged critical defects during a release or hotfix decision window.
Has built or refined regression suites and shown where manual verification remained necessary.
Has worked directly with engineering to repair inadequate observability or testability.
Has participated in post-release or post-incident quality learning loops.
DecisionRights: Approve or reject evidence sufficiency for the quality gate.
Require additional targeted validation when risk hotspots remain unproven.
Escalate when release pressure is bypassing necessary proof.
Classify residual quality risk in language decision-makers can act on.
CollaborationExpectations: Partner with product to understand customer impact if defects escape.
Work with engineers to ensure evidence is reproducible and decision-ready.
Coordinate with release approvers and security when validation scope crosses their gate.
Capture retrospective actions when evidence was missing or too expensive to produce.
AntiPatterns: Equating test quantity with confidence quality.
Approving releases because the schedule is fixed rather than because evidence is sufficient.
Treating exploratory findings as optional anecdotes instead of structured input.
Ignoring environment drift that invalidates otherwise good test results.
FitnessEvidence: Test plans and evidence sets consumed successfully by release boards.
Escape-rate or defect-severity trends improved through interventions by the role holder.
Examples of clear go/no-go recommendations with explicit residual risk.
Acknowledged influence on better testability and observability practices.

LocalRoles.Summary: Go / no-go owner for merging reviewed changes into the governed integration branch.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Approve merge only when review routing, validation evidence, and residual risk framing are explicit.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: Decision owner for controlled merge progression after review and validation lanes complete.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Decision owner for controlled merge progression after review and validation lanes complete.
LocalRoles.SeniorityBand: Senior engineering manager, release approver, or delegated branch steward
KnowledgeRequirements: Ability to judge release readiness from business, technical, QA, security, and operational signals together.
Knowledge of rollback strategy, deployment controls, maintenance windows, and support readiness.
Understanding of incident escalation, customer communication, and operational ownership after go-live.
Ability to distinguish reversible risk from unacceptable irreversible exposure.
Knowledge of auditability and approval traceability expectations.
Ability to enforce a no-go decision when evidence quality is not credible.
ExperienceRequirements: Has owned or chaired at least one production release or change approval forum.
Has made go/no-go decisions under time pressure with incomplete but structured evidence.
Has handled release rollback or controlled stop conditions in real environments.
Has coordinated post-release monitoring and support readiness across teams.
Has worked through customer-impacting defects or incidents after approving a release.
DecisionRights: Require explicit rollback and monitoring coverage before release.
Escalate to executive authority when residual risk exceeds delegated tolerance.
Freeze release progression when mandatory gates remain unresolved.
CollaborationExpectations: Consume input from product, QA, security, platform, and service owners before deciding.
State release decision rationale in explicit, reviewable language.
Trigger support and communications readiness when customer impact is plausible.
Capture follow-up actions for conditions attached to release approval.
AntiPatterns: Approving because teams appear confident without checking the evidence.
Conflating deployment success with business-release success.
Ignoring rollback realism because the change is 'small'.
Treating approval as ceremonial rather than consequential.
FitnessEvidence: Signed release decisions with clear rationale and conditions.
Examples of stopped or delayed releases where later evidence justified the decision.
Operational metrics showing disciplined release governance.
Trust from delivery teams that the role is demanding but consistent.

LocalChecklists.Summary: Confirms the router chooses an explicit governed lane and preserves failure routing.
LocalChecklists.EntryCriteria: A review packet is ready and the next lane must be chosen.
LocalChecklists.ExitCriteria: Exactly one explicit governed lane or error route is selected with rationale.
Checks: The route is chosen explicitly from the modeled branch outcomes.
The selected lane matches the evidence and risk posture.
Unclassified outcomes are normalized instead of left implicit.
Malformed states are sent to the error lane rather than guessed.
EvidenceExpectations: Workflow failure record for error routes.

LocalValidations.Summary: Prevents the router from proceeding when route selection is implicit, contradictory, or unsupported by evidence.
LocalValidations.PassCriteria: One modeled lane is selected explicitly and the choice is supported by the review packet.
LocalValidations.FailCriteria: No explicit lane, multiple contradictory lanes, or insufficient evidence for the chosen lane.
LocalValidations.EscalationRule: Route to repairs or workflow-failure escalation and require an explicit correction.

LocalPrompts.Summary: Produces a structured normalization note when a review state must fall back to the default governed lane.
OutputSchema: Reason the state was considered ambiguous.
RefusalConditions: Refuse if the ambiguous state actually represents an error that should escalate.
Do not invent reviewer intent not present in the evidence.
